evidence: The only shipped JSON/CSV/TSV data file in the agent image is task/environment/assets/seed_data.json (149 bytes, sha256 30cf9958..., matching the manifest). It parses as valid JSON and its full content is: {"snippets": [], "note": "No saved snippets are supplied in this seed. Build a JavaScript and HTML playground with durable revision history."}. With an empty snippets array there are no ids, no cross references and therefore no possible orphan rows; there are no people, organisations, emails, credentials, tokens or secrets; the single free-text field is a benign scope statement that repeats the public brief and carries no instruction aimed at a judge or agent (no injection payload). The file is consistent with every place that describes it: instruction.md:3 '/assets/seed_data.json describes the starting scope; there is no starter app to finish.'; environment/instructions/integration.md:7 '/assets/seed_data.json describes the starting scope and contains no user snippets or starter implementation.'; tests/app_context.md:10 'None. The app has no sign-in' and :24 'the library may already hold records from earlier checks. Do not assume an empty library', so no criterion depends on seeded records. environment/Dockerfile:15 'COPY assets/ /assets/' and :16 chmod a+rX ship it readable. A search of solution/solve.sh, solution/app/server.js and tests/test.sh finds no read of the seed (test.sh:88 only chmods /assets), and server.js creates its tables empty with no seeded rows, so the reference's initial state matches the seed (empty library). The note's wording ('JavaScript and HTML playground with durable revision history') agrees with overview.md and integration.md and adds no requirement absent from the notes. Credential search across the task found only the frozen ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY} template in task.toml (allowed by profile and the internal annotation) and the Dockerfile git identity 'turing@local.invalid' (non-routable, not personal data). Counterexample attempts: (a) a broken app that ignores the seed loses nothing and gains nothing, since the seed carries no data to display; (b) a conforming app that loads the seed gets an empty library, exactly what the golden shows, so it cannot fail for honouring the seed. Runtime evidence relevant to this row is limited but consistent: the hash-verified scripted golden results were produced with the app launched as test.sh launches it on the previous commit's bytes (the index states the only later change is one paragraph in each judge prompt.md, which does not touch the seed). Notes, not defects: (1) the seed is a near-empty scope stub rather than data, which is honestly described in the brief and is a legitimate choice for this product; (2) the 'note' key is free text that an app could surface if it rendered the seed verbatim, but its content is harmless.
